# 1 Samuel Chapter 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 153r | **Source Image:** 1SA_005_page_001.jpg

---

**1** After the Philistines captured the ark of God, they carried it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.

**2** They brought it into the temple of Dagon and placed it beside their god's statue.

**3** When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, there was Dagon — fallen flat on his face on the ground in front of the ark of the LORD. They picked Dagon up and put him back in his place.

**4** But when they got up early the next morning, Dagon had fallen face-down before the ark of the LORD again — and this time his head and both his hands had been broken off and were lying on the threshold. Only the trunk of the idol remained.

**5** That is why, to this day, the priests of Dagon and everyone who enters Dagon's temple in Ashdod will not step on the threshold.

**6** The LORD's hand fell heavily on the people of Ashdod. He devastated them and afflicted them with tumors — both the city and the surrounding territory.

**7** When the people of Ashdod saw what was happening, they said, "The ark of the God of Israel cannot stay here with us. His hand is crushing us and our god Dagon."

**8** So they summoned all the Philistine rulers and asked, "What should we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" The rulers answered, "Move it to Gath." So they moved the ark of the God of Israel to Gath.

**9** But after they moved it there, the LORD's hand struck that city too, throwing it into a terrible panic. He afflicted the people of the city — young and old alike — with an outbreak of tumors.

**10** So they sent the ark of God on to Ekron. But as soon as it arrived, the people of Ekron cried out, "They've brought the ark of the God of Israel here to kill us all!"

**11** They urgently summoned all the Philistine rulers and pleaded, "Send the ark of the God of Israel back where it belongs before it kills us and our people!" For a deathly panic had gripped the entire city; God's hand was devastatingly heavy there.

**12** Those who didn't die were afflicted with tumors, and the city's cry of anguish rose all the way to heaven.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **5:3-4 — Dagon's progressive humiliation**: The narrative uses dark humor to devastating theological effect. Day one: Dagon falls prostrate before the ark — the pose of worship. Day two: Dagon is dismembered, his head and hands severed on the threshold. The God of Israel doesn't just defeat Dagon; He systematically demolishes him.

2. **5:4 — "only the trunk remained"**: The Hebrew דָּגוֹן may pun on דָּג (fish), the lower fish-form of the hybrid deity. Everything human about the idol — its head (thought) and hands (power) — is destroyed. Only the monstrous remainder is left.

3. **5:6 — "tumors"**: The Hebrew text has a Ketiv-Qere: the written text reads 'ofalim (swellings/tumors), while the reading tradition has tehorim (hemorrhoids). The LXX also mentions mice destroying the land. The plagues echo Egypt — God proving His sovereignty on foreign soil.

4. **5:7-12 — the ark's circuit**: The narrative traces the ark from Ashdod to Gath to Ekron with devastating consequences at each stop. What the Philistines captured as a trophy becomes an uncontrollable weapon. The captors become the captives.

5. **5:12 — "rose all the way to heaven"**: The chapter ends with a cry ascending to heaven — an ironic reversal. In chapter 4, Israel cried out in defeat. Now the Philistines cry out under the weight of the very God they thought they had conquered.

— PNEUMA
